data.narrative:
Varda Space Industries, a Series D-stage space and aerospace company founded by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov, commands a current valuation of $1.58B following $329M in total raised capital. The valuation assessment draws from a comparative set spanning five public-market Space & Aerospace comps (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and eight private peers including Impulse Space, Apex Space, and others at comparable or adjacent funding stages.

Two valuation methods triangulate a defensible range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.5x step-up multiplier to the $1.5B last post-money valuation, implying $2.2B. Peer-median analysis across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies—Sierra Space ($8.0B), Impulse Space ($4.3B), Apex Space ($2.3B), and Skyryse ($1.1B)—yields a median of $3.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (sector median 24.4x) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, typical for private companies.

The triangulated valuation range is $1.9B–$3.8B, with a median of $2.8B. This implies 12–140% upside from current valuation. Key uncertainties include stage-specific progression assumptions and the wide dispersion in peer valuations ($1.1B–$8.0B), which likely reflects differing technology maturity, customer traction, and capital efficiency across the portfolio. Revenue visibility would meaningfully constrain this range.
